title: Upgrade Maestro: cohort sequencer and transactional migration runner for Private
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Scope: build the Upgrade Maestro—a cohesive sequencer + transactional migration runner for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that performs orchestrated upgrades with safety gates, LTS channel pinning, and observable migration steps. This ticket is focused on the control-plane components and runbooks required to perform schema, config, and agent binary upgrades across cohorts without leaving services in a partially-incompatible state.

Motivation: customers on Private install ask for predictable, auditable upgrade behavior with minimal downtime. Existing ad-hoc scripts and manual steps are error-prone in multi-cluster environments and do not capture dependency-aware ordering (eg. metadata service -> runtime agents -> DB migrations). Upgrade Maestro should reduce operator toil and provide deterministic rollouts with automatic rollback on safety signal failures.

Deliverables:
- Sequencer service that accepts an upgrade proposal and breaks it into ordered phases (preflight -> canary cohorts -> staged rollout -> finalization).
- Transactional migration runner that executes idempotent, reversible schema and resource migrations with checkpoints and resumability.
- Canary/cohort definition model (size, isolation level, health probes) and default cohort heuristics tuned for private installs.
- LTS channel mapping rules so installs pinned to LTS channels only transition to compatible patch trees unless explicitly opted-in.
- Preflight compatibility probes: binary compatibility, API surface matrix, KB/agent version matrix, and KMS/cert checks.
- Runbook templates and a dry-run harness to validate migration plans against a snapshot of cluster state.
- Telemetry hooks and dashboards for tokenized rollout traces, per-step latency, failure modes, and post-upgrade verification.

Non-goals: the ticket does not include new agent-side migration code (only the runner invocation and sequencing), nor changes to on-prem provisioning APIs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sequencer accepts a JSON upgrade proposal and emits an ordered phase plan that can be inspected via API. 2) Migration runner executes a synthetic dry-run plan against a staging snapshot and produces a deterministic report. 3) Canary cohort logic supports at least two isolation modes (single-host, cross-host microcohort) and aborts rollout on defined health thresholds. 4) LTS mapping prevents non-compatible major/minor upgrades unless ‘force’ flag is used and a guard is recorded in audit logs. 5) End-to-end demo: upgrade a 3-node private cluster from runtime-1.18 -> runtime-1.19 with a schema migration and show automatic rollback on induced KV-commit failures.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: sequencer (stateless API + persistent plan store), planner (phase generator from compatibility matrix), executor (migration runner + step orchestrator), verifier (post-step health probes), and audit log writer. Plans are versioned; each step has idempotency tokens and checkpoint markers stored in the plan store (Postgres).

Migration runner: supports SQL migrations via transactional wrapping where possible, file-format upgrades (blob migration with mark-and-sweep), and binary agent rolling updates (drain -> update -> smoke test -> uncordon). A two-phase commit style pattern will be used for cross-service state transitions where possible.

Safety gates: preflight success, canary pass rate >= 99.5% for defined probes, failure budget checks, and resource availability checks (GPU/CPU/disk) before each phase.

Compatibility matrix: maintain a simple CSV-driven matrix stored alongside releases mapping (control-plane-version, agent-min, agent-max, schema-version). The planner will refuse transitions that violate matrix unless override flag with auditor sign-off is present.

Storage & state: plan-store schema must support plan.history (stringified events), step.checkpoint (string tokens), and .resume_token. We will reuse existing private control-plane Postgres schema with migration to add plan tables.
rollout_plan:
1) Prepare: generate upgrade proposal via CLI and run preflight; 2) Dry-run: execute plan in dry-run mode against snapshot; 3) Canary: deploy to cohort A (5% hosts) with enhanced observability; 4) Progressive: use geometric growth of cohorts (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with health gating; 5) Finalize: run final verification and mark plan complete.

Canary gating: health probes include API latency SLO checks, error rate thresholds, KV commit success ratio, and consumer backpressure signals. If any probe exceeds threshold for >2 consecutive minutes we abort and trigger rollback.
rollback_plan: Built-in rollback steps per phase. For schema migrations: attempt reversible migration path; if not reversible, quiesce traffic, restore from snapshot and replay pre-upgrade WAL until point-in-time before migration. For agent binary upgrades: drain -> previous-binary redeploy -> smoke tests -> uncordon. Rollback will emit an incident ticket template and attach plan logs. Automatic rollback triggers: failed health probe, resource exhaustion, >10% customer-visible error rate increase.
telemetry: Emit structured events for: plan.created, plan.phase.started, plan.phase.completed, step.started, step.completed, step.failed, rollback.initiated, rollback.completed. Include plan_id, step_id, cohort_id, cluster_id, and trace_id. Send metrics to telemetry pipeline and create a Grafana dashboard (dashboard ID: private-upgrade-990001). Create SLO alert rules for canary failures and prolonged stuck states (>10m).
